stories.title: Dodgers Lose Their 6th Straight — Crow-Armstrong Beats Them with Two HRs

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
The Dodgers' losing streak: now 6 games. Season-high.

Pete Crow-Armstrong: 2 HR, 4 RBI.
Shohei Ohtani: leadoff HR No. 29 as a Dodger — passes Davey Lopes for 2nd all-time in franchise history.

Dodgers still lose. 7-6.

#Dodgers #Cubs

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
69-45. Still first in the NL West.

But the Dodgers have been swept in back-to-back series and lost six straight — leaving 8 runners on base last night alone.

For the best team in baseball, this is a genuine wobble.

#Dodgers

facebook.long_form:
The Los Angeles Dodgers entered 2026 as the World Series favorite. They're now on a six-game losing streak — a season high — after falling to the Chicago Cubs 7-6 on Wednesday night.

Pete Crow-Armstrong hit two home runs and drove in four runs to lead the Cubs. Shohei Ohtani hit a leadoff home run, his 29th as a Dodger, passing Davey Lopes for second place on the franchise's all-time leadoff home run list. It extended his hitting streak to nine games. It still wasn't enough.

The Dodgers left eight runners on base. They've now been swept in consecutive series — their second straight sweep. The skid raises real questions about a team that, not long ago, looked unbeatable.

At 69-45, they're still atop the NL West. But baseball doesn't care about projections. Six games is six games.
facebook.image_caption: Six straight losses for the Dodgers. Pete Crow-Armstrong went deep twice Wednesday night in a 7-6 Cubs win. Shohei Ohtani hit a leadoff homer — his 29th — but it wasn't enough. Season-high six-game losing streak for LA. 🔵

stories.title: Matt Olson Passes Stan Musial — 8th All-Time in Consecutive Games

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Matt Olson just passed a Hall of Famer.

His 896th consecutive game Wednesday put him ahead of Stan Musial (895) — sole possession of 8th all-time in MLB history.

The streak started May 2, 2021. In Oakland.

#Braves

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
While Olson's streak hit 896:

🔹 Bryce Elder: 7 innings, 1 hit allowed
🔹 Drake Baldwin: 2 RBI
🔹 Atlanta: 7th straight win (season-high)

The Braves are playing good baseball on both sides of the equation.

#Braves

facebook.long_form:
On Wednesday, Matt Olson did something that doesn't happen often: he passed a Hall of Famer on one of baseball's most revered lists.

Olson played in his 896th consecutive game as the Atlanta Braves beat the Miami Marlins 4-1, moving past Stan Musial (895 consecutive games) into sole possession of 8th place on MLB's all-time consecutive games played list. The streak began May 2, 2021 — when Olson was still with the Oakland Athletics.

Musial is one of the greatest hitters in baseball history. Passing him on any list means something. But consecutive games played is a different kind of record — it's about showing up, every day, regardless of how you feel, for years.

Olson has done exactly that. He shows no signs of stopping.

Bryce Elder added to the moment with seven innings of one-hit ball. Drake Baldwin drove in two runs. The Braves extended their winning streak to seven games — a season high — and Olson was in the middle of all of it.
facebook.image_caption: Matt Olson played in his 896th consecutive game Wednesday — passing Stan Musial for 8th all-time in MLB history. The streak started in 2021 in Oakland. It's still going. ⚾🔒

article.headline: Matt Olson Passes Stan Musial with 896th Consecutive Game, Moves Into 8th All-Time

stories.title: Sonny Gray Is 14-2 — Red Sox Are 30-5 Since June 25

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Sonny Gray: 14-2. AL wins leader.

The Red Sox beat the White Sox 4-0 Wednesday — Wilyer Abreu's 20th home run, Gray's sixth scoreless inning.

Boston is now 30-5 since June 25.

#RedSox

facebook.long_form:
Sonny Gray blanked the Chicago White Sox over six innings Wednesday, striking out eight while allowing just three hits and two walks. His record: 14-2. The American League lead in wins, and it isn't particularly close.

Wilyer Abreu went 2-for-3 with three runs scored and his 20th home run of the season. The final score: Red Sox 4, White Sox 0.

Boston is now 30-5 since June 25 — one of the most remarkable sustained surges in baseball this season. They've won seven consecutive games. The rotation is deep. The bullpen has been elite. And Gray, at 14-2, has been the story all season long.

The White Sox still lead the AL Central by three games, but the American League is watching what Boston is building.
facebook.image_caption: Sonny Gray goes to 14-2. The Red Sox are 30-5 since June 25. Seven-game win streak. Wilyer Abreu's 20th home run. Boston is running hot right now. ⚾🔥

stories.title: Angel Genao Makes Guardians History — 4 Hits in His MLB Debut

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Angel Genao went 4-for-4 in his MLB debut Wednesday.

First player in Cleveland Guardians franchise history to record four hits in an MLB debut.

The Guardians still lost 6-5 on a ninth-inning error.

#Guardians

facebook.long_form:
Angel Genao's MLB debut was historic. It also ended in a loss.

In the Cleveland Guardians' 6-5 defeat to the New York Mets on Wednesday, Genao recorded four hits — becoming the first player in Cleveland Guardians franchise history to accomplish that in an MLB debut. That's a franchise that dates back to 1901. No one had done it before.

But the Mets tied the game in the ninth inning when Guardians shortstop Brayan Rocchio fumbled a bases-loaded grounder by A.J. Ewing, allowing Jared Young to score with two outs. The Mets went on to win 6-5.

Genao's debut was exceptional by any measure. The box score just doesn't show that.
facebook.image_caption: Angel Genao: 4 hits in his MLB debut. First in Cleveland Guardians franchise history to do it. The team still lost 6-5 on a ninth-inning error. Historic debut. Tough night. ⚾

stories.title: Field of Dreams Game — 7 Days Away, Phillies vs. Twins on Netflix

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Field of Dreams. Phillies vs. Twins. Netflix.

August 13. Dyersville, Iowa.

Schwarber has 33 home runs. Arraez is in the lineup with a career .329 average.

Seven days out.

#Phillies #Twins

facebook.long_form:
Seven days from now, the Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins will walk out of a cornfield in Dyersville, Iowa — and this year, for the first time, the world will be watching on Netflix.

The 2026 Field of Dreams Game is August 13, and it comes loaded with storylines. Kyle Schwarber, who has 33 home runs this season, brings the NL's most compelling home run chase. Luis Arraez, who was acquired at the trade deadline and carries a career .329 batting average — three batting titles to his name — adds a different kind of baseball drama to the Philadelphia lineup. The Phillies also added Logan Raley at the deadline.

For the Twins, this is a chance to step into one of baseball's most magical settings on a stage larger than any regular-season game.

The Field of Dreams Game is one of the best things baseball does. Seven more days.
facebook.image_caption: Phillies vs. Twins. August 13. Dyersville, Iowa. The Field of Dreams Game streams live on Netflix for the first time this year. Schwarber (33 HR) and Arraez (.329 career) headline the matchup. Seven days out. 🌽⚾
